title: Learn How To Backspin | Power Move Basics | Beginner Breaking Tutorial

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher uses a direct, instructional approach, breaking down complex movements into manageable, sequential steps. He emphasizes both the physical mechanics and the necessary safety precautions for each move.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher introduces himself and the move.
Teacher explains the two parts of the move: the kick and the roll.
Teacher explains how to get to the floor and the importance of arching the back.
Teacher guides the viewer through the move in slow motion.
Teacher focuses on the leg whip.
Teacher gives advice on clothing for the move.

cues: pull your knees to your chest
common_mistakes: spinning on the mid or lower back
safety: wear a slippery jacket to create less friction

steps_taught.name: Backspin
steps_taught.description: A power move where the dancer spins on their back.

what_hinders: the transition between the kick and the roll is fast

quotes.text: You want to make sure you're on your shoulders, too.
If you are left-handed, you should be rolling to your left.
You want to make sure that you're on your shoulders, not your mid or lower back.
Your body needs to be symmetrical, meaning it's the same on both sides.
You want to wear a slippery jacket, meaning something like a windbreaker or sweater.

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher performs a backspin on a concrete surface.
The teacher sits on the floor and demonstrates the arching of the back.
The teacher demonstrates the roll to the shoulder.
The teacher demonstrates the push-off and the leg kick.
The teacher demonstrates the tucking of the knees.
The teacher performs the full backspin in a studio.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher explicitly advises on the type of clothing (slippery jacket) to reduce friction, which is a practical, non-movement-based tip for success.
